findings.exact_text: Arda swung free on the line Nisa still held.
findings.reason: He cut the line away from the bridge while it looped his harness; Nisa holding the line he's swinging on is unclear, and the rescue mechanics conflict.
Line was cut away, yet Nisa still holds it and hauls him; then the line is declared lost. Contradictory logic about what was cut.

findings.exact_text: Their gliders still lay where the old knotted trunk leaned, just as they'd left them.
findings.reason: Glider was lashed to a trunk and Arda unfastened the line; the gliders' position near knotted trunk is plausible but the line is later lost, and Nisa's glider was never described landing.

findings.exact_text: They reached the bridge too late.
findings.reason: Bridge was already torn loose and later they cross it with the line; the 'too late' framing is clear, but 'could no longer carry them' then says it's still sagging above a drop, and the line crossing across the gap is inconsistent with anchor-trunk placement.

findings.exact_text: Ten minutes, and we watch the sun; we want to be back before dusk.
findings.reason: Dusk reference is awkward and introduces a time frame inconsistent with corridor-light urgency; Nisa returns after far less.

findings.exact_text: while the island that had dissolved into the cloud wall lived on in the journal and the tag only he and Nisa could explain.
findings.reason: Ending ends on an abstract clause instead of the tag image; also claims they can explain the tag, which they cannot.

findings.exact_text: The bridge was sinking, and the line was still looped around his harness.
findings.reason: Line was anchored to trunk and held by Nisa; 'looped around his harness' reads awkwardly and conflicts.

findings.exact_text: he cut the line away from the sinking bridge.
findings.reason: Line was anchored to a trunk, not the bridge; phrasing is confusing.

findings.exact_text: "We have to hurry to the bridge," he said.
findings.reason: Followed by 'too late' with no cause; bridge failure feels unmotivated and the sequence is abrupt.

findings.exact_text: On the far side of the bridge, from a cliff edge, he could look out
findings.reason: The stacked opening location phrases create a compressed, awkward spatial construction; stating that he reached the cliff edge makes the position immediately clear.
The pronoun “it” has an imprecise physical referent here. Naming the camp produces the natural English object of “search” and improves immediate clarity.

findings.exact_text: She leaned out and hauled, his hand found her wrist
findings.reason: A comma incorrectly joins two independent clauses, making the rapid action sequence grammatically unstable. A semicolon preserves the pace and clarifies the progression.

target_segments.source_text: "Ten minutes, and we watch the sun; we want to be back before dusk.
On the far side of the bridge, from a cliff edge, he could look out over the whole interior, and what he saw stopped him cold: the old knots didn't stop.
Nisa caught up and followed him in despite everything, because whatever she thought of him right now, she wasn't going to let him search it alone.
"We have to hurry to the bridge," he said.
They reached the bridge too late.
The bridge could no longer carry them.
The bridge was sinking, and the line was still looped around his harness.
There was only one thing left to do, and he hated every second of it: he cut the line away from the sinking bridge.
The bridge fell away beneath him into the cloud sea, and Arda swung free on the line Nisa still held. She leaned out and hauled, his hand found her wrist, and her grip found him.
Their gliders still lay where the old knotted trunk leaned, just as they'd left them.

Then he took out the glider-tag and held it in his open palm, turning it so the unknown name caught the sunset, and wondered who had tied those knots, and whether they had ever made it home—while the island that had dissolved into the cloud wall lived on in the journal and the tag only he and Nisa could explain.
